why.title: Why now
why.1.d: Every password reset costs support time and some users never come back. Passkeys turn the loop into one device prompt.
why.2.d: WebAuthn binds each credential to your RP ID, so a look-alike domain cannot use it. Stolen passwords stop being the default way in.
why.3.d: iOS, Android, Windows and macOS already prompt for Face ID, fingerprint, PIN or a security key. Your users have seen it before.

tpl.tree.title: Archive layout
tpl.tree.lede: Open any item to see its purpose and a short excerpt. Code blocks have a copy button.
tpl.f1.what: A small Next.js app you can run locally and copy from: sign-up with a passkey, sign-in, a settings page to list and revoke keys, and recovery codes. Server code uses @simplewebauthn/server; the browser side uses @simplewebauthn/browser.
tpl.f1.l1: Route handlers for registration and authentication options + verification
tpl.f1.l2: Challenge store with expiry, plus a session cookie after login
tpl.f1.l3: Settings screen: list, rename, revoke passkeys
tpl.f1.l4: Recovery codes: generate, hash, show once, redeem
tpl.shot.cap1: Illustrative HTML render of the example app's settings screen, not a product screenshot.
tpl.f2.what: Steps for adding passkeys next to existing Supabase password accounts, so current users keep working while they enrol a passkey.
tpl.f2.s1: Create the passkeys table with row-level security
tpl.f2.s2: Offer "add a passkey" after a normal password login
tpl.f2.s3: Let enrolled users sign in with a passkey first, password as fallback
tpl.f2.s4: Optionally hide the password field once a user has two passkeys
tpl.f3.sum: Keep Clerk or move out: a decision note
tpl.f3.what: If you already use Clerk, this note helps you decide whether to keep it and turn on its passkey option, or move auth into your own database.
tpl.f3.k1: its built-in passkey option covers what you need
tpl.f3.k2: you rely on its user and organisation management UI
tpl.f3.m1: you must own the credential table and session format
tpl.f3.m2: pricing per active user no longer fits your plan
tpl.f4.what: Thirty checks to run before you turn passkeys on in production, grouped by config, ceremony, storage, UX, recovery and operations.
tpl.f5.what: A matrix of browsers, operating systems and flows to test by hand, with a column for passkey autofill (conditional UI).
tpl.f5.note: The boxes are empty for you to tick. The $499 plan includes a filled-in record for your app.
tpl.f6.what: A short commercial licence: use the code in your own products and client work, but do not resell the template itself.

pv.title: Privacy policy
pv.lede: What PassGate collects, why, and who else sees it. Short version: only what we need to answer you and deliver what you buy. We never sell personal data.
pv.s1.p: PassGate (passgate.incidental.site) is a product of Incidental AI. Incidental AI decides how the data described here is used.
pv.s2.l1: Interest form: your email, the plan and stack you pick, and your language.
pv.s2.l3: Purchases: Creem tells us your email, the name you entered, the plan, the amount and an order reference. We never see your card details.
pv.s2.l4: Install service: the repository access and project details you choose to share for the job.
pv.s3.p: We use Cloudflare Web Analytics, which sets no cookies, and our own first-party event counter at stats.incidental.site. It records page views, clicks, scroll depth and form events, without your name or email. We use it only to see which pages work.
pv.s3.p2: Your browser's local storage keeps your language and theme choice. There are no advertising trackers or advertising cookies on this site.
pv.s4.l1: To reply to you, and to tell you when checkout opens if you asked.
pv.s4.l2: To deliver your order, provide support and handle refunds.
pv.s4.l3: To send the newsletter, only if you subscribed. Every issue has an unsubscribe link.
pv.s4.l4: To protect the forms from spam and abuse.
pv.s5.p: We do not sell or rent personal data. We share it only with the services that run PassGate: Creem (Armitage Labs OÜ), our merchant of record, for payments, tax and receipts; Cloudflare for hosting, data storage and email routing; and our email delivery provider for the messages we send. Creem keeps its own records as tax law requires, under its own privacy policy.
pv.s6.p: Interest and newsletter entries are kept until you unsubscribe or ask us to delete them. Order records are kept as long as accounting and tax rules require.
pv.s7.p: You can ask to see, correct or delete your data at any time. Email us from the address you used and we will act on it within 30 days. You can also contact your local data protection authority.
pv.s8.p: If we change this policy, we update this page and the date at the top.
